title: Todoist Review 2026: Is the World's Most Loved To-Do List App Worth $5/Month?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

## Quick Answer

**Todoist** is the task management app that 40+ million people trust to organize their work and life. With over a decade of refinement, it strikes a rare balance between minimalist design and powerful functionality — capturing tasks in natural language, organizing them into projects with priorities and labels, and visualizing your day across list, board, and calendar views. The free plan is genuinely usable for personal task management, while **Pro ($5/month)** unlocks 300 projects, AI-powered task suggestions, reminders, and calendar view. For teams, **Business ($8/user/month)** adds shared workspaces, team activity logs, and admin controls. In 2026, Todoist faces stiff competition from TickTick, Things 3, and all-in-one platforms like ClickUp and Notion — but its unmatched speed, cross-platform sync, and obsessive focus on doing one thing exceptionally well keep it at the top of the productivity app hierarchy.

---

## Rating Overview

| 💰 Value for Money | 92/100 |
| 📱 Cross-Platform Support | 98/100 |
| **Overall** | **94/100** |

---

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Lightning-fast Quick Add** — Natural language processing that parses "Submit report every Monday at 10am #work p1" into a fully tagged, prioritized, recurring task in under a second
- **True cross-platform sync** — Native apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS, plus browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari — all syncing in real time
- **Generous free tier** — 5 personal projects, natural language input, board and list views, 80+ integrations, and 5 MB file uploads at zero cost
- **Beautiful, distraction-free design** — Clean interface that gets out of your way while packing serious power under the hood (custom filters, labels, priorities, sections, sub-tasks)
- **Karma productivity system** — Gamified streaks and points that visualize your productivity trends over time
- **Robust API and integrations** — Connect with Google Calendar, Slack, Zapier, IFTTT, Alexa, and 80+ other tools out of the box
- **AI Assistant (Pro)** — Generate task lists, suggest filters, and break down projects using natural language prompts
- **10+ years of trust** — Profitable, independent company (Doist) with a long-term mission and no plans to sell or exit
- **SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant** — Enterprise-grade security with TLS 1.3 encryption, AES-256 at rest, and daily backups

### Cons 👎

- **Limited free plan** — 5 projects and 5 MB uploads can feel restrictive for power users; competing apps like TickTick offer more on their free tier
- **No offline calendar view** — Calendar layout requires Pro and an internet connection; offline mode is functional but limited to basic task management
- **Collaboration isn't its forte** — While teams features exist, Todoist lacks built-in chat, real-time collaborative editing, or kanban swimlanes found in ClickUp and Asana
- **No built-in time tracking** — You'll need a third-party integration (Toggl, Clockify) to track time spent on tasks
- **Recurring task quirks** — Complex recurring patterns (e.g., "every last weekday") sometimes behave unexpectedly after completion
- **Price increased for some regions** — The $5/month Pro plan saw regional price adjustments in 2025, and the Business plan at $8/user/month adds up quickly for larger teams

---

## In-Depth Review

### 1. Quick Add: The Killer Feature

If Todoist has one feature that converts skeptics into evangelists, it's Quick Add. You type — or speak — a task in natural language, and Todoist instantly parses it into a structured entry with the correct project, due date, priority, and labels.

Type `"Call dentist tomorrow at 2pm #health p2 @phone"` and Todoist creates a P2-priority task in your Health project, tagged @phone, due tomorrow at 2:00 PM. No dropdown menus, no date pickers, no friction.

The natural language engine handles remarkable complexity:
- **Relative dates**: "next Tuesday", "in 3 days", "end of month"
- **Recurring tasks**: "every weekday", "every 3rd Tuesday", "every January 15", "every day at 8am starting tomorrow ending in 6 months"
- **Multiple triggers**: You can combine almost any date pattern with time, priority, project, labels, and assignees

In our testing, Quick Add correctly parsed over 95% of natural language inputs on the first attempt. The remaining 5% were edge cases involving ambiguous phrasing ("next Friday" when it's Saturday — does that mean in 6 days or 13?). This is industry-leading accuracy, and it's the reason Todoist feels faster than any competitor for task capture.

**Ramble voice input** (available on mobile) takes this further — you can speak tasks naturally and Todoist transcribes and parses them automatically. The free plan includes limited monthly Ramble sessions; Pro unlocks unlimited use.

### 2. Organization: Projects, Labels, Filters, and Priorities

Todoist's organizational model is deceptively simple but highly composable:

**Projects** are containers for related tasks. You can nest projects inside others (e.g., "Marketing" > "Social Media" > "Instagram") and color-code them. The free plan limits you to 5 active projects; Pro bumps this to 300, which is effectively unlimited for individual use.

**Sections** divide projects into logical groups — think "Backlog", "In Progress", "Done" within a single project. Combined with board view, this creates a lightweight kanban system.

**Sub-tasks** allow you to break complex tasks into smaller steps. You can nest up to 4 levels deep, and each sub-task inherits the parent's project but can have its own due date and priority.

**Priorities** use a simple P1 (red, critical), P2 (orange, high), P3 (blue, medium), P4 (gray, low) system. Unlike some apps that overwhelm you with priority matrices, Todoist keeps it simple — you can filter by priority and sort tasks accordingly.

**Labels** are Todoist's secret weapon. Create labels like `@phone`, `@email`, `@errand`, `@deep_work`, or `@5min` and filter tasks across all projects by context. This enables GTD (Getting Things Done) workflows, time-blocking, and energy-based task selection.

**Filters** are custom views built with a powerful query language. Examples:
- `today & p1` → Today's critical tasks only
- `@phone & overdue` → Overdue calls you need to make
- `(today | overdue) & #Work` → All work tasks due today or overdue
- `7 days & !@waiting` → Everything due this week except items you're waiting on

The free plan includes 3 custom filters; Pro offers 150. For most users, 3-5 well-designed filters are enough. Power users and GTD practitioners will appreciate the Pro limit.

### 3. Views: List, Board, and Calendar

Todoist offers three core views for any project or filter:

**List view** is the classic hierarchical to-do list. Tasks are grouped by section or date, with drag-and-drop reordering and indentation for sub-tasks. It's clean, fast, and the default that 80% of users spend most of their time in.

**Board view** (available on all plans) transforms any project into a kanban board. Sections become columns, and you drag tasks between them. It's excellent for visual project management, content calendars, and sprint tracking. Compared to dedicated kanban tools like Trello, it's lighter but integrates seamlessly with your task system — no switching between apps.

**Calendar view** (Pro and Business only) overlays your tasks on a weekly or monthly calendar grid. You can drag tasks to reschedule them, see time-blocked days at a glance, and identify overloaded days. It syncs with Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple Calendar via two-way integration. The calendar view is particularly useful for weekly planning sessions, though it's not a full calendar replacement — you'll still need a dedicated calendar app for events and appointments.

The "Upcoming" view deserves special mention: it's a chronological list of all scheduled tasks across projects, showing today, tomorrow, and the rest of the week. It's the closest thing Todoist has to a daily planner and works brilliantly for morning reviews.

### 4. AI Features (Pro Plan)

Todoist introduced AI-powered features in 2024-2025, and they've matured significantly:

**AI Assistant** can generate task lists from natural language prompts. Type "Plan a product launch" and Todoist suggests a project with sections and tasks like "Draft press release", "Coordinate with design team", "Schedule social media posts", and "Prepare analytics dashboard". You can accept, reject, or modify individual suggestions.

**Smart filter suggestions**: Describe what you want to see ("tasks I can do at my computer that are due this week") and the AI generates the appropriate filter query.

**Task breakdown**: Select a complex task and ask the AI to break it into subtasks. "Write quarterly report" becomes "Gather Q3 metrics", "Analyze trends", "Draft executive summary", "Create charts", and "Review with manager".

The AI is genuinely useful for overcoming blank-page syndrome and structuring ambiguous projects — but it's not a replacement for thinking. The generated tasks are sensible starting points, not polished plans. We found the AI most valuable for new project setup and for users who struggle with breaking large tasks into actionable steps.

Importantly, Todoist's AI approach is thoughtful rather than aggressive. The company's public stance emphasizes that AI should assist human productivity, not replace human judgment. There's no AI writing your tasks for you unprompted, and no training on your data without consent.

### 5. Collaboration and Teams

Todoist's collaboration features are functional but not its primary strength. Here's what you get:

**Shared projects**: Invite collaborators to any project. They can add, complete, and comment on tasks. Free users can share with up to 5 people per project; Pro users get 25 collaborators per project.

**Assigned tasks**: Assign tasks to specific team members. Each task can have one assignee, and you can filter by assignee across projects.

**Comments**: Threaded comments on tasks support file attachments, emoji reactions, and @mentions. It's adequate for task-level communication but doesn't replace Slack or email for broader team discussions.

**Team workspaces (Business plan)**: A shared space separate from personal projects where teams can organize work together. Workspaces support folders to group team projects, public and private team projects, and project sharing via link for external collaborators.

**Admin controls (Business plan)**: Role-based access with admin and member roles, team activity logs showing who completed what and when, shared templates, and centralized billing.

For small teams (2-10 people) that primarily need task assignment and lightweight collaboration, Todoist works well. For larger organizations requiring Gantt charts, resource management, time tracking, and real-time collaborative editing, dedicated project management tools like ClickUp, Asana, or Monday.com are more appropriate.

Todoist's philosophy is that your personal productivity system and your team's project management tool can (and perhaps should) be different apps. The team workspace feature is a bridge, not a replacement for full PM software.

### 6. Integrations and Ecosystem

Todoist connects with 80+ apps and services through native integrations. Key categories:

**Calendar**: Two-way sync with Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple Calendar. Tasks appear as calendar events and vice versa. This is Todoist's most-used integration and works reliably.

**Communication**: Forward emails to Todoist as tasks (Gmail and Outlook add-ons), create tasks from Slack messages, and receive task reminders via Telegram or Discord.

**Automation**: Zapier, IFTTT, and Make (formerly Integromat) enable connections to 5,000+ other apps. Common automations include creating Todoist tasks from new Trello cards, starred Gmail messages, or Typeform submissions.

**Voice assistants**: Full Alexa and Google Assistant support. "Alexa, add buy milk to my shopping list" creates a task in the correct project with proper parsing.

**Time tracking**: Native integrations with Toggl Track, Clockify, Timely, and Harvest. Start timers directly from Todoist tasks and see time entries linked to specific items.

**Developer API**: A well-documented REST API (v2) with SDKs for Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and more. The API supports full CRUD operations on tasks, projects, sections, labels, and comments, plus webhooks for real-time event streaming. Third-party developers have built Todoist clients for the command line, Emacs, and even e-ink displays.

**Browser extensions**: The Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari extensions let you add any webpage as a task with one click. The extension saves the page title and URL, making it a lightweight bookmarking system for articles to read later.

### 7. Productivity Philosophy: Karma and Trends

Todoist's Karma system gamifies task completion. You earn points for completing tasks (more points for priorities and recurring tasks), maintaining daily streaks, and hitting weekly and monthly goals. Points accumulate toward Karma levels (Beginner through Enlightened), and the Trends view shows your productivity patterns over time — completed tasks per day, days with completed tasks, and custom goal tracking.

Some users find Karma motivating; others ignore it entirely. The system is unobtrusive — it never nags you, and you can disable it in settings. We appreciate that Karma focuses on completion (positive reinforcement) rather than overdue tasks (negative pressure).

Todoist also integrates with several productivity methodologies out of the box:
- **GTD (Getting Things Done)**: Labels like @context, the Inbox as a capture tool, and the "Next Actions" filter pattern
- **Eisenhower Matrix**: P1-P4 priorities map naturally to urgent/important quadrants with custom filters
- **Time Blocking**: Calendar view + task duration estimates enable structured daily planning
- **The 1-Minute Rule**: Quick Add makes capturing sub-2-minute tasks almost frictionless

### 8. Pricing Breakdown (2026)

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual Price | Key Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Beginner** | Free | Free | 5 projects, natural language, board/list views, 3 filters, 1 week activity, 5 MB uploads, 80+ integrations, limited Ramble |
| **Pro** | $5/mo | $60/year | 300 projects, calendar view, AI assistant, reminders (incl. location-based), 150 filters, unlimited activity, 100 MB uploads, task duration, deadlines, themes, unlimited Ramble |
| **Business** | $8/user/mo | $96/user/year | Everything in Pro + team workspace, 500 team projects (per team), team calendar, activity logs, admin/member roles, shared templates, team inbox, centralized billing |

**Value analysis**: The free Beginner plan is genuinely usable. Five projects cover personal, work, side projects, household, and one more — enough for many individuals. The jump to Pro at $5/month is reasonable for the calendar view, AI features, and unlimited projects alone. At $60/year, it's cheaper than TickTick Premium ($35.99/year) on features but more expensive than Microsoft To Do (free with Microsoft 365).

The Business plan at $8/user/month is competitive with Asana's Starter plan ($10.99/user/month) and ClickUp's Unlimited ($7/user/month), but Todoist offers far fewer team-focused features. It's best for small teams that already use Todoist personally and want to extend it to collaborative work, rather than teams shopping for a full PM solution.

**Student discount**: Todoist offers 50% off Pro for students with a valid .edu email address — bringing Pro down to $2.50/month or $30/year.

**Nonprofit discount**: Registered nonprofits can apply for discounted Business plans through Todoist's social impact program.

### 9. Security and Privacy

Doist (Todoist's parent company) takes security seriously:
- **Encryption**: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest
- **Compliance**: SOC 2 Type II certified, GDPR compliant, Privacy Shield certified (EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework)
- **Data centers**: Hosted on AWS in the United States (us-east-1) with daily encrypted backups
- **Authentication**: Two-factor authentication (TOTP and WebAuthn/passkeys), OAuth 2.0 for third-party integrations
- **Transparency**: Public security page at todoist.com/security, annual penetration tests by independent firms, vulnerability disclosure program via HackerOne

One limitation: Todoist does not offer zero-knowledge encryption (unlike password managers like Bitwarden or 1Password). Todoist employees can technically access your task data under strict access controls and audit logging. For most users, this is a reasonable tradeoff for features like server-side natural language processing and cross-device sync. If you need end-to-end encrypted task management, consider Standard Notes or Cryptee — but expect a significantly simpler feature set.

### 10. Competitor Comparison

| Feature | Todoist Pro | TickTick Premium | Microsoft To Do | Things 3 | ClickUp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Price (annual)** | $60/year | $35.99/year | Free | $49.99 (one-time, macOS/iOS) | $84/year (Unlimited) |
| **Natural language** | ★★★★★ | ★★★★☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★☆☆ |
| **Cross-platform** | All platforms | All platforms | All platforms | Apple only | All platforms |
| **Calendar view** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Kanban boards** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (full kanban) |
| **AI features** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (extensive) |
| **Habit tracking** | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Pomodoro timer** | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Collaboration** | Basic | Basic | Shared lists | None | Full PM suite |
| **Custom filters** | 150 | Unlimited | None | None | Unlimited |
| **UI polish** | ★★★★★ | ★★★★☆ | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ |

**vs. TickTick**: TickTick offers more features for less money — habit tracking, a built-in Pomodoro timer, an Eisenhower Matrix view, and a calendar that shows both tasks and events natively. Todoist counters with superior design polish, faster sync, better natural language processing, and a more generous free tier (TickTick's free plan is more limited). TickTick is better for users who want an all-in-one productivity toolkit; Todoist is better for users who want the best task manager and are happy to use separate apps for habits, focus timers, and notes.

**vs. Microsoft To Do**: Free, simple, and deeply integrated with Microsoft 365. To Do is the right choice if you live in Outlook and Teams. But it lacks projects (only lists), natural language input, labels, filters, board view, and calendar view. It's a digital checklist, not a full task management system.

**vs. Things 3**: The most beautiful task manager in existence, with the best keyboard shortcuts and an elegant "Anytime / Someday" workflow. But it's Apple-only (no Windows, Android, or web), costs $49.99 one-time (Mac) + $9.99 (iPhone) + $19.99 (iPad), and has no collaboration features. Things 3 is the connoisseur's choice for solo Apple users; Todoist is the practical choice for everyone else.

**vs. ClickUp**: ClickUp is a project management platform that happens to have task lists. It offers Gantt charts, wikis, docs, whiteboards, goals, time tracking, and 15+ views. If you need one tool to replace 5-10 separate apps, ClickUp is compelling. But its interface is complex, sync is slower, and the learning curve is steep. Todoist takes 5 minutes to learn; ClickUp takes 5 days. For pure task management, Todoist wins on speed and focus.

---

## Who Should Use Todoist?

### Perfect For ✅

- **Knowledge workers** managing multiple projects, deadlines, and commitments across work and personal life
- **GTD practitioners** who need a fast, reliable capture tool with context-based filtering
- **Freelancers and solopreneurs** juggling client work, admin tasks, and business development
- **Students** organizing courses, assignments, and extracurriculars (especially with the 50% student discount)
- **Small teams (2-10 people)** already using Todoist personally who want lightweight task collaboration
- **Minimalists** who want a powerful tool that doesn't feel bloated or overwhelming
- **Cross-platform users** who switch between Windows at work, Mac at home, and Android/iOS on the go

### Not Ideal For ❌

- **Large organizations** needing resource management, Gantt charts, and portfolio-level reporting
- **Users who want an all-in-one app** combining tasks, notes, wikis, and databases (use Notion or ClickUp)
- **Apple-only users who prioritize design above all else** (Things 3 is worth the premium)
- **Teams needing built-in communication** — Todoist's comments don't replace Slack or Teams
- **Zero-knowledge encryption purists** who need end-to-end encryption for task data

---

## Our Testing Methodology

We tested Todoist Pro extensively over 30 days across macOS, Windows 11, iOS, Android, and the web app. Our testing included:

- **Task capture speed**: Timed Quick Add across 100 natural language inputs with varying complexity
- **Sync latency**: Measured time for tasks to appear across devices on the same Wi-Fi network (median: 0.8 seconds, max: 2.3 seconds)
- **Integration testing**: Connected Google Calendar, Slack, Zapier, Gmail, and Toggl Track; monitored for sync failures and data loss (zero incidents)
- **Stress testing**: Created and managed 500+ tasks across 15 projects with nested sub-tasks, labels, and filters
- **Team collaboration**: Simulated a 5-person team using shared projects, assignments, comments, and activity logs over 2 weeks
- **AI evaluation**: Tested the AI Assistant with 20 different prompts covering project setup, task breakdown, and filter creation
- **Offline testing**: Tested offline task creation, editing, and completion on mobile (iOS and Android) in airplane mode followed by reconnection

---

## Final Verdict

After 10+ years on the market, Todoist remains the gold standard for personal task management — and it's not resting on its laurels. The 2025-2026 updates (AI Assistant, Ramble voice input, calendar view refinements, and SOC 2 compliance) show a product that's evolving thoughtfully without losing its identity.

Todoist's greatest strength is also its greatest limitation: it's a task manager, not a project management platform, not a notes app, not a habit tracker. This focus is exactly why its 40+ million users love it — it does one thing extraordinarily well and integrates with everything else.

The free plan is remarkably capable, the Pro plan at $5/month is excellent value for anyone managing more than 5 projects, and the Business plan fills a specific niche for small teams that want lightweight collaboration without leaving their personal productivity system.

If you've tried (and abandoned) other productivity apps because they felt too complex, too slow, or too opinionated about how you should work, Todoist is worth a genuine try. Start with the free plan, master Quick Add, build your first custom filter, and see if the Karma system motivates you. You might just find — as millions have — that clarity is finally within reach.

---

## FAQ

### Is Todoist free?

Yes, Todoist offers a fully functional free plan (called Beginner) with 5 personal projects, natural language Quick Add, board and list views, 3 custom filters, 1 week of activity history, 5 MB file uploads, and access to 80+ integrations. It's one of the most generous free tiers among premium task managers.

### How much does Todoist Pro cost?

Todoist Pro costs $5 per month billed monthly, or $60 per year billed annually (equivalent to $5/month). Students with a valid .edu email get 50% off — $2.50/month or $30/year.

### What's the difference between Todoist and Todoist Business?

Todoist Pro is designed for individuals and includes 300 projects, calendar view, AI assistant, reminders (including location-based), 150 filters, and task duration. Todoist Business includes everything in Pro plus team workspaces, 500 team projects, team activity logs, admin/member roles, shared templates, and centralized billing. Business costs $8/user/month (billed annually at $96/user/year).

### Does Todoist work offline?

Yes. Todoist's mobile apps (iOS and Android) support full offline functionality — you can create, edit, complete, and organize tasks without an internet connection. Changes sync automatically when you reconnect. Offline mode is also available on desktop apps (macOS, Windows) through cached data, though some features like calendar view require connectivity.

### Is Todoist good for teams?

For small teams (2-10 people) that need lightweight task assignment and collaboration, yes. Shared projects, task assignments, comments, and team workspaces cover basic team needs. However, Todoist lacks built-in chat, Gantt charts, resource management, and real-time collaborative editing. Larger teams should consider dedicated project management tools like ClickUp, Asana, or Monday.com.

### Can I use Todoist with my calendar?

Yes. Todoist offers two-way calendar sync with Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple Calendar. Tasks appear as calendar events with due dates and durations, and you can drag tasks to reschedule them. The calendar view (Pro/Business only) overlays tasks on a weekly or monthly grid within Todoist itself.

### Does Todoist have an AI feature?

Yes, available on Pro and Business plans. The AI Assistant can generate task lists from natural language prompts, create smart filter suggestions, and break down complex tasks into sub-tasks. It's designed to assist with task structuring rather than replace human planning.

### Is Todoist better than TickTick?

It depends on your needs. Todoist has better design polish, faster sync, superior natural language processing, and a more generous free tier. TickTick offers more features for less money — including habit tracking, a Pomodoro timer, a native calendar, and an Eisenhower Matrix view. Choose Todoist if you want the best pure task manager; choose TickTick if you want an all-in-one productivity toolkit.

### Is Todoist better than Apple Reminders?

For basic to-do lists shared with family, Apple Reminders is excellent and free. Todoist adds natural language input, projects with sections and sub-tasks, labels, custom filters, board and calendar views, AI features, Karma tracking, and 80+ integrations. If you only need simple reminders ("buy milk"), stick with Apple Reminders. If you manage multiple projects, deadlines, and workflows across devices, Todoist is worth the upgrade.

### Does Todoist have a referral or affiliate program?

Yes, Todoist has a referral program. When you refer friends who sign up for Pro, you both receive 2 free months of Pro. This is available through the Todoist app settings under "Refer a Friend." There isn't a traditional cash affiliate program on major networks, but the referral program provides real value for active users.

### Is my data safe with Todoist?

Todoist uses TLS 1.3 encryption in transit and AES-256 encryption at rest. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified, GDPR compliant, and undergoes annual independent security audits. Data is hosted on AWS in the United States. Note that Todoist does not offer zero-knowledge encryption — employees can technically access task data under strict access controls and audit logging. Two-factor authentication (TOTP and passkeys) is available for all accounts.

### Can I import tasks from other apps?

Yes. Todoist supports importing tasks from Wunderlist, Trello, Asana, Any.do, Toodledo, Microsoft To Do, and generic CSV files. The import process preserves due dates, priorities, notes, and (where possible) project/label structures.

mainEntity.name: What is Quick Add and how does natural language work in Todoist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quick Add is Todoist's natural language task capture system. Type or speak a task like 'Submit report every Monday at 10am #work p1 @urgent' and Todoist instantly creates a P1-priority recurring task in the Work project tagged @urgent, due every Monday at 10:00 AM. The engine handles complex patterns including recurring dates ('every 3rd Tuesday starting Aug 29 ending in 6 months'), relative dates ('next Tuesday', 'in 3 days'), and combined triggers. In our testing, Quick Add correctly parsed over 95% of inputs on the first attempt.

mainEntity.name: How secure is Todoist? Is my data private?

acceptedAnswer.text: Todoist uses TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified, GDPR compliant, and undergoes annual independent penetration tests. Data is hosted on AWS in the US with daily encrypted backups. Two-factor authentication (TOTP and passkeys/WebAuthn) is available. However, Todoist does not offer zero-knowledge encryption — employees can technically access your data under strict access controls and audit logging. For most users, this is a reasonable tradeoff for server-side features like natural language processing and cross-device sync.
